summary.intent: Run the GSD manager to discuss and kick off parallel planning for all 5 remaining hardening-block phases (51–55) of the v1.1 milestone, overlapping discussion with background planning agents to parallelize work from one terminal.
summary.outcome: All 5 phases (51–55) had context discussions completed and CONTEXT.md files committed on isolated branches. Phases 51 and 52 were fully planned (4 and 5 plans respectively, plan-checker passed). Phases 53, 54, and 55 had worktrees created and planners spawned by end of session.

repo: The GSD dep parser misreads 'Phase 49 **(v1.1 baseline)**' as two deps (49 + phantom '1.1'), causing phases 51–55 to appear dep-blocked even though they only depend on Phase 49 (complete). This silences recommended_actions entirely.
Phase 50 had a stale is_active: true flag in the init query output despite being marked [x] completed in ROADMAP.md and shipped in PR #527 — state file lags ROADMAP on certain completion paths.

The GSD commit helper auto-switches the working tree branch on the first phase-specific commit (main → feat/<phase-slug>), which pulls the branch out from under any concurrently-running background agent operating in the same tree.

core.hooksPath is an absolute path pointing to the main worktree's .husky directory, so all git worktrees run the same pre-commit hook (husky/lint-staged) and require node_modules to be present independently.
The gsd commit helper can report commit_failed as a false negative — the commit actually lands and git log must be checked to verify.

Phase 51's todo #15 (logger redaction + Faro transport) was incorrectly scoped into the crypto-signature hardening phase; the acceptance criteria require Faro to verify redaction, making it a no-op without a transport. Deferred to a future observability phase.

Phase 53's #16 pin-clearing machinery was correctly identified as a symptom-fix for force-push clobbering the release-please bot commit, not an independent cause. Dropped in favor of fixing recompute reliability.
The canonical ref path for the phase 51 todo was slightly stale — todos live under .planning/todos/pending/ not the path captured in the original CONTEXT.md.

Phase 52 D-04 resolved to encrypting the FUSE filename (not omitting it) because FileMetadata has no name field, making omission unreconstructable — the CONTEXT fallback was correct and the planner found it independently.

Background general-purpose agents on Claude Code DO have the Agent tool (Tools: *), so they can nest sub-agents. The manager.md guardrail claiming otherwise is stale/conservative for this harness configuration.

Phase 51 scope locked to S1/S2/S3 IPNS crypto-signature work only. Key decisions: embedded-vs-DTO anti-rollback (409 on embedded > DTO seq), fail-closed verification (return false not throw), exhaustive S3 key zeroization sweep across SDK + Rust unwrap paths with lint/test enforcement.

workflow: Parallel phase planning requires isolated git worktrees per phase — without isolation, the GSD commit helper's auto-branch-switch pulls the tree out from under a running background agent.
Worktrees need their own node_modules (via real pnpm i, not symlink) because core.hooksPath points to the main tree's .husky and lint-staged needs local node_modules to run.
Symlinking node_modules into a worktree is fragile and should be avoided; pnpm i in the worktree is the correct approach even if slower.
Session/usage limit interruptions leave worktree state intact — background agents can be restarted cleanly from where they left off since pnpm i had already completed.
Three parallel planning worktrees (p51, p52, p53) can run concurrently without git lock collisions because each worktree has an independent index.
The pattern for safe parallel phase work: main tree stays on main (free for discussing the next phase), each active phase gets its own worktree on its feature branch.

The GSD manager workflow's 'Claude Code cannot nest sub-agents in background' guardrail should be verified against the actual agent registry before being trusted — general-purpose agents with Tools: * do support nesting.

Discussing all remaining phases before planning any of them maximizes parallelism: all five CONTEXT.md files were captured in series during the inline discussion loop, then planners were spawned in parallel.

friction: GSD dep parser phantom-dep bug: '(v1.1 baseline)' annotation in ROADMAP phase header caused phases 51–55 to appear dep-blocked, suppressing all recommended_actions and requiring manual workaround.
Phase 50 stale is_active flag in init query output caused misleading dashboard state even though the phase shipped.
Session/usage limit interrupted the Phase 51 planner after ~31 seconds (mid-startup), requiring a clean restart at the reset moment.

Manager.md's 'no nested subagents in background on Claude Code' guardrail was stale — caused initial unnecessary back-and-forth about whether to run plan inline vs. background before the user correctly challenged it.
First background planner spawned without worktree isolation, requiring a stop-relaunch cycle to set up proper isolation before it had done meaningful work.
The gsd commit helper's false-negative commit_failed reporting required a git log verification step after every significant commit.
Symlink node_modules approach was tried and abandoned — one extra round-trip to discover pnpm i is the correct approach.

No automated detection that a background agent is about to commit into a shared tree while the foreground is also committing — the collision risk was caught manually by the user asking about worktree isolation.
open_items: Todo #15 (web logger redaction interceptor + Faro transport wiring) deferred from Phase 51 to a future observability phase — needs a dedicated phase once a Faro/monitoring strategy is decided.

Phase 53 force-push discipline as primary fix for the release-please stale-pin loop — lightweight self-correction net (re-run preview on final state, revisit cancel-in-progress) left as optional planner-evaluated safeguard.
Phase 55 Tier 3 security-sensitive crypto files have no tests — test coverage must be written before any refactoring begins on those files.
Phases 52 and 53 planners were still running at session end; phase 53 had just started pnpm i / research.
Worktrees for phases 54 and 55 were being created at the very end of the session — planners not yet spawned for those two.
All 5 hardening-block feature branches (51–55) will need to be merged back to main after execution — potential conflicts on shared .planning/STATE.md and ROADMAP.md.

GSD dep parser phantom-dep bug with parenthetical annotations in phase headers (e.g. 'Phase 49 **(v1.1 baseline)**') should be reported/fixed upstream to prevent future suppression of recommended_actions.
Phase 54 migration decision: use ts-node or tsx for runtime invocation of the migrated helpers — deferred to planner to pick based on what's already in the monorepo.
